raw.details:
24 hours. One real farm problem. One room full of people trying to solve it.

Most hackathons ask you to build another app for people like you. This one asks you to build for the people who feed the country. Drones that spot-crop stress. Rovers that spray with precision. A voice assistant that answers a farmer in their own language. If you can build it, there is probably a field that needs it.

Agri-Tech Hackathon is a national-level, 24-hour offline sprint hosted by K. J. Somaiya School of Engineering, Mumbai, and organised by e-CESA. Software and hardware builds are both welcome.

Last edition, in numbers and names

  • 1,772 registrations on Unstop
  • ₹2,00,000 prize pool
  • First place: Team Snack Overflow, D. J. Sanghvi College of Engineering, for an automated tractor-mounted sprinkler system
  • Partners included BKT, LIC, NABARD, Festo, KIAAR, Red Bull and Domino's

Why register

  • The prize pool is now ₹3,50,000, up from ₹2,00,000 last edition.
  • Registering is free, and Round 1 is just an abstract and a short pitch video you can record from anywhere.
  • You don't need an agriculture background or prior AI, IoT or blockchain experience.
  • Round 1 is about how you think: write your abstract on any of the five themes. For the sprint, problem statements go live 3 to 4 days before the event on our website, grouped by tech bucket.
  • Mentors stay with you during the sprint, and the organisers provide food and snacks.
  • You pitch your build to a panel of industry and academic judges.

Eligibility

  • Undergraduate and postgraduate students, any discipline
  • Teams of 3 to 4 members; cross-college and cross-specialisation teams allowed

Themes

  • Next-Gen Agri-Tech: robotics, drones, computer vision, IoT, AI and predictive analytics
  • Agri-Market Access: direct marketplaces, demand forecasting, blockchain traceability, smart storage and quality grading
  • Farmer Empowerment: multilingual AI, offline-first tools, hyperlocal advisories and AR/VR training
  • Green Growth: soil regeneration, water conservation, carbon monitoring and climate intelligence
  • Open Innovation (Round 1 only): your idea, your solution, as long as it serves agriculture

Rounds

Round 1: Abstract Submission (online)

Submit a 5 to 6 page abstract (maximum) as a PDF, proposing your own solution under any of the five themes, along with an unlisted YouTube video link (5 to 7 minutes) explaining your solution in simple terms, as if pitching to a farmer who has never seen it before. This checks your oratory and pitching skills, since your solution ultimately has to be understood by farmers on the ground. Teams are shortlisted for Round 2 based on the abstract and the video.
Deadline: 27 December 2026, 11:59 PM IST. Shortlist announcement: 7 January 2027.

Round 2: The 24-Hour Sprint (offline, at KJSSE)

Shortlisted teams from Round 1 move directly into Round 2, no separate registration needed.

Dates: 28 to 29 January 2027 (Thursday to Friday).

Prizes

Total prize pool: ₹3,50,000

  • Winner: ₹1,50,000 + certificate
  • First Runner Up: ₹1,20,000 + certificate
  • Second Runner Up: ₹80,000 + certificate

Rules

  • Projects must be built for this hackathon. Pre-existing projects are not allowed.
  • Each team submits one abstract.
  • Team members cannot be changed after registration is finalised.
  • Participants bring their own laptops, hardware, tools and development environments.
  • The organisers' decision is final.
  • Partners, sponsors, prizes, dates and other details mentioned here are subject to change; the latest confirmed information will always be on this page and our official website.
